Aug 2026 • Family

A fantastic (mostly) Vietnamese food selection which you can order from the menu or do a walk around to see and choose what you would like prepared, which adds a uniqueness to the dining experience. Unacceptable service!
Jul 2026 • Family
The restaurant is cosy and the food is quite fine, but the service is terrible! My family and I have traveled through Vietnam for 3 weeks and we have never experienced such poor service. 

We chose the restaurant as it looks very cozy and nice from the outside. When we first got a table, we noticed that there was incredibly much noise, but that is how it is. Our waitress understood very little English so we had to order by showing the menu tab. We repeated several times that we wanted dumpings without fish and the waiter nicked. 

The waiting time for the food was very long and got the food/drinks completely shifted, so some had to wait to get their drink for 35 minutes. We never got all our food and what we got was not right. We tried several times to address the staff, but were just answered with a flabet comment and provocative attitude. We end up just canceling the rest, as 1 hour has already passed. When we finally catch up with a leader, he disagrees with our experience and we still have to pay for getting the wrong food!

We may have ended up in the wrong place at the wrong time, but that is absolutely unacceptable!

Overpriced and not worth it
Jul 2025 • Family
We went here last year, and had a decent good experience. This time around - not so much. 

Prices here are on the higher end of the city. But we did know that coming here.

Food was okay - some of it. We order a bò nhúng dấm, which they said would be for 3-4 people, maybe even 5 or 6. We order two for eight of us and did have starters as well. But I’d say each of those servings would be for a maximum of 3, and some of us had to get extra food on the way back to the hotel. And to top it off, this dish is served with a dipping sauce for which we received two bowls of sauce split between 8 people 😅

This dish was mediocre. Normally you would have the pot on the middle of the table. But here they did it for you, and everything was overcooked.

But the two incidents which was really disappointing was:

- we ordered drinks for the whole table, and we counted them with the server after the order to check we had 11 drinks for 11 people.

When the drinks came out we had 12 drinks, one extra smoothie of 120K VND. If was a discussion back and forth and they insisted we ordered it. To close the discussion we just ended up taking it (and paying for it).

So when it came to the bill, and we had to pay for 11 Wet wipes when we only used 5, they were told to pull it back out.

Had they just apologized and taken it upon them with the drink without insisting that we did order 12 drinks and making up different excuses, I would have just have picked it up. Even though I would say this would normally have been on the house.

Based on this, I doubt I will be coming back

Ngon Restaurant is a hidden gem that masterfully showcases the rich and diverse flavors of Vietnamese cuisine in an elegant yet welcoming setting. Whether you’re a fan of traditional dishes or looking to explore something new, Ngon offers a dining experience that’s both authentic and refined.

Ngon’s atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between sophistication and warmth. The restaurant features a modern, stylish interior with a nod to Vietnamese culture through its décor. Earthy tones, wooden accents, and tasteful lighting create a cozy yet upscale vibe. Whether you’re there for a casual meal or a special occasion, Ngon provides a comfortable and aesthetically pleasing environment.

The menu at Ngon is impressive, with a wide array of traditional Vietnamese dishes presented with a contemporary twist. From the iconic pho to flavorful bun bo Hue and crispy banh xeo, every dish bursts with authentic flavors and fresh ingredients. The grilled lemongrass pork and spring rolls are standout appetizers, perfect for sharing and full of aromatic spices.

Ngon takes pride in the presentation, with each dish beautifully plated, elevating the dining experience. The balance of flavors, from savory and sweet to spicy and tangy, is masterfully executed, staying true to Vietnamese culinary traditions while adding a modern touch. The portions are generous, and the freshness of the herbs and spices is unmistakable.

While Ngon is slightly more upscale compared to casual Vietnamese eateries, the quality of the food, ambiance, and service more than justifies the price. It’s an excellent value for money, especially given the care that goes into every dish and the generous portion sizes.

While my guests we already looking at the menu to choose desserts (an hour had passed) the waiter came to me again informing me the dish I selected (fish in banana leaves) was fished too. 

At that point I really started to get irritated, but nevertheless I ordered another dish from the Thai menu ( red curry chicken). The waiter apologized to me and took also the order for desserts for my guests. 

After 10 minutes the deserts came in and my guests started eating. After 15 minutes when my guests were finishing their last dishes the waiter came back to tell me the food was finished and I would not be able to have dinner anymore. 

I called the manager and told him that I did not get any food and I was hosting the dinner. He smiled and apologized and brought me the bill.

Concluding this experience I told him I really felt bad and disappointed. As the highest ranking officer of the Netherlands government I always took fellow officials to the restaurant. My friend and an old time Saigon resident, took us to the Nha Hang Ngon restaurant in Pasteur Street to sample the local cuisine. The restaurant is actually an old converted French villa which has been meticulously restored to its past glory.

Fine Vietnamese Food Close to Saigon’s Cathedral
Mar 2015 • Couples
The French tradition of fine baked bread and delightful restaurants continues to this day in Ho Chi Minh City, or Saigon as it was traditionally called and is still referred to by most of the locals. An excellent choice in terms of food, service, and outdoor ambience is Nha Hang Ngo located at 160 Pasteur. Finding addresses is easy in Saigon due to the switch to a western alphabet that the French colonial masters imposed in the early 20th century. Just head toward the river from the Cathedral and take a right at the end of the square. A block later you encounter Pasteur. Take a left and the restaurant is at 160 on the left a little ways later. You’ll notice the open front with tables arranged under colonial columns and overhead balconies. Even though you are also likely to see a crowd for lunch or dinner there is a lot of seating so you should be shown to a table without an undue wait. As for what to order it hardly maters as everything we tried was excellent. Pick from several kinds of Pho, that diverse variety of Vietnamese soups, and a number of seafood entries. Ginger Crab, as is true in my much of Southeast Asia, including Hong Kong and Singapore, is excellent. I’d suggest you look at what other diners are eating, ask for recommendations, and be adventurous. For a treat head to the toilet in the back and notice all the items along the way that have been prepped for cooking. I had no idea what many of them were but they should give you ideas. Eating out is a joy in this old French Capital regardless of it’s current status as an officially Communist but effectively capitalist economic system.

Different and Novel
Sep 2014 • Friends
Having read a number of the more critical reviews, I wanted to clarify what Nha Hang Ngon is about.
If you are simply looking to eat cheaper and better Vietnamese food, then go elsewhere. If what you're after is a romantic, more private evening in air-conditioned surrounds, again don't bother.
What Nha Hang Ngon rightly prides itself on is its colourful, noisy ambience, attended by an eclectic customer base locally and internationally.
Its water piece in the centre of the restaurant adds to the pleasure, and the building is a lovely example of ex-colonial architecture.
Don't just sit at a table and order from the menu; wander around the food stalls that pepper its perimeter; get a feeling for the diversity of foods on offer from various Vietnam regions, and appreciate how the dishes are prepared/cooked; then sit down and enjoy.
That is the best way to appreciate the place and leave with a sense of fulfilment, both from the cultural and culinary perspectives!

Smile but do tell them if you don't want something or don't like something. 

The first night 1 dish never came but we ordered too much anyway so we didn't bother. Another dish came wrong and they tried to sell it to us but we insisted on sending it back and they replaced it straight away. In a busy place like this mistakes can happen. This is a country where people are not used to the concept of international hospitality yet so it may take some time until service is up to western standard.

More than half of the clientele is local so it shows you the food is authentic. Service is quite fast as they are all prepared in the stands in front of you. Menu is long so if you can't be bothered to order from menu, just go to the food stalls and point at it. This is a good way to try street food and to be sure there is certain standard of hygiene. 

Not all waiters speak English so you may need to be patient when ordering . On my second visit our waitress was outstanding. Good English, very personal, and you can see she is good at her job. The first night we were not so lucky. 

The restaurant is a big colonial house. In the evening when the lights are lit in the garden the atmosphere is really nice. I would definitely recommend a visit. It's not a complete lie either to say that I will do anything for really good street food, including squatting in a short dress in 90+ degree weather, slurping on hot & spicy soup while perspiring enough sweat to add favor to the bite I'm swallowing. If you think that's disgusting, I'm probably quietly judging you for not being an authentic street food lover.

There are times though, when squatting on the streets just isn't ideal, like when you're trying to catch up with childhood friends you haven't seen for 20 years or when you're trying to have a first romantic brunch with your Mr. in your home country. These are the times that I'm thankful for Saigon having restaurants like Quán Ngon.

The atmosphere of this eatery is beautiful, set inside an airy two-story villa-style property on the swanky avenue of Pasteur. Silk tents cascading over tables circle around a peaceful pond in the middle, it's hard to believe there's such an oasis in hectic Ho Chi Minh. 

There are food stands all around the restaurant, replicating the street food experience with the safety of culinary gentrification and prices to match. The food is good and there are plenty of dishes too authentic for my Las Vegas chinatown to offer. I confess to love the air-conditioning, frugal but enough to enjoy my bún mắm. The Mr. claims the egg rolls are the best he's ever had, the quality of the rice paper superb and the fillings are made of never-frozen-before meats and seafood. If you're in District 1, it's definitely worth a visit.

For high-quality photos of this restaurant, you can go here http://inspirationsalongtheway.blogspot.com/2013/01/ngon-ngon-ngon.html

First impressions: Acting on a tip from our local tour guide, we sought out this little gem. It is the sister concept restaurant of the one in Hanoi (26 Tran Hung Dao, Hanoi) -- they use the same name and logo, although I'm not sure which came first. Offering cheap, tapas-style, street food in a normal-height-seat restaurant setting, it is of excellent value. Grade A-minus.

Pros: For a visitor, it's a good introduction to Vietnamese cuisine. This place has many outdoor tables. The atmosphere, though plainly busy, is laid back. Several cooking stations are lined up along the side of the restaurant, each with its own particular set of dishes they made. From a highly-extensive menu, you can choose from a wide range of dishes and desserts. A very close competitor to my usual favourite: Red Bean Slushee, the three-coloured dessert drink was heavenly. Upon returning home, I sought it out from every Asian store/restaurant I can find.

Cons: Though the food is quite tasty, my Vietnamese friend swears it's not exceptional. In fact, she insists that, for certain dishes, she can find better ones at a cheaper price --- elsewhere!
Another downside relates to dinginess. (This is where the Hanoi restaurant gains a 1/2-star for its cleaner, neater Old French villa setting.) While service is good, it is the first thing that suffers when it gets very busy. Arrive real early as wait times can extend to 45 minutes. And watch out for sudden downpours if you are seated outside (that's when it can get vermin-ugly in a hurry).

Verdict: For a first-timer, it's worth a visit, if you can reserve beforehand, arrive early and able to see past the dinginess. Frankly, between the two, I prefer its Hanoi sister site.

A bit overrated...

If what you're looking for is an atmospheric tourist lunch experience, Ngon is a great place. Set in what is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful colonial French era buildings in town, the semi-open air set-up is charming, and the fact that all the food is cooked in sections wrapped around the bottom floor where you can watch the staff prep and cook the food is also a winner.

The price is also outstanding. Really, it gets more and more difficult these days to find this kind of tourist-oriented restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City that offers meals at such an incredibly low price. You'll hear no complaints from me about the cost.

The issues for me are the service and the flavor of the food. This restaurant is very, very, very busy, especially at lunch time, and the staff seem to have an attitude that they will get to you eventually, and if you're displeased with the service they have rows of people waiting for a table and it's not going to hurt them in the long run if you decide not to come back. Also, since such a large percentage of their customers are tourists, they don't expect it's likely you'll be back anytime soon anyhow. I wouldn't say that they are rude, they're just not attentive, and getting a refill on a drink or just simply getting the attention of a waiter can be a task. They'll come, they'll take your order, they'll bring your food, they'll give you the bill. You really can't expect more. The food is definitely clean - that's a bonus here in Vietnam. Since you can literally walk over and watch them prepare your food after you order it, you can feel comfortable that the cooking areas are clean and the ingredients are fresh. But... it's just bland! In a town where you can easily find cheap, simple dishes that are just exploding with traditional flavors, the emphasis at Ngon seems to be all on show, and not on substance.

In short, the restaurant is beautiful, the atmosphere is interesting and traditional, and the food is clean and pretty. But they won't pay much attention to you, and you probably won't feel like you've had the most amazing meal of your life.
